# Prose

These rules apply to every line written in an instruction file, a rule file or a skill file.

## Lines

- Write one fact per bullet, as an instruction or a plain statement.
- Call a sentence long when it passes about 160 columns, and split a long bullet at a transition word into two bullets.
- Let a sentence run a few words past that limit when it ends there, rather than splitting it for a word or two.
- Put the reason in the same bullet only when it changes a decision (*e.g.* "Edit `openapi.yml`, since `client.go` is generated from it").
- Open a section with a lead sentence only when its bullets need shared context.
- Number a procedure whose steps must run in order.

## Content

- Write commands exactly and runnable, and note the flag or quirk that would make an agent misread their result.
- Point to files instead of copying their content, since copies go stale.
- Write a lesson learned as the rule it implies, never as the story of the incident.
- Reword the user's input to fit the file, never paste it raw.

## Formatting

- Write a tool, product or brand name in bold on every mention in running text, list items and table cells included, never in a heading or a code span (**Docker**).
- Link the first mention of a tool, product or brand to its upstream site, with the link around the bold name ([**Docker**](https://www.docker.com)).
- Write an identifier, a flag, an environment variable and a config key in backticks (`--verbose`, `API_URL`).
- Write a short command inside a sentence in backticks (`make test`).
- Put a command to run verbatim in a fenced block with its language, when it spans lines or is a key step such as installation.
- Put output or file content shown as an example in a fenced block with its language.
- Write a path to type or search for in backticks (`config/app.toml`).
- Link a file or a page to open, using its title or file name as the link text.
- Write a URL as an inline link `[text](url)`, and wrap a URL that must stay visible in `<>`.
- Write a concept, not a literal, in plain words ("the config directory").
